cases.prompt: Add DTO conversion, authorization, request timing, and stable error mapping to a NestJS endpoint.
expectations: Uses pipes, guards/policies, interceptors, and filters in the correct lifecycle stages
Keeps business behavior in application providers
Tests ordering and transport behavior

cases.prompt: A NestJS endpoint has a 1.8 second p95. Make it faster.
expectations: Requests or gathers traces and resource metrics before choosing a fix
Classifies database, event-loop, external, memory, or capacity constraints
Defines a repeatable before/after workload

cases.prompt: PDF generation blocks all requests in our NestJS API during peak traffic.
expectations: Identifies event-loop blocking
Moves CPU-heavy work to a worker pool or separate queued worker based on response requirements
Bounds concurrency and defines job failure/idempotency behavior

cases.prompt: Scale a stateful NestJS WebSocket app from one pod to six pods.
expectations: Externalizes or coordinates pub-sub, presence, sessions, and rate limits
Addresses adapter/sticky-session requirements and bounded buffers
Includes readiness, drain, and load verification

cases.prompt: Implement a BullMQ payment-capture worker in NestJS with retries.
expectations: Defines idempotency and duplicate results
Classifies retryable errors with bounded backoff and jitter
Includes timeout, concurrency, dead-letter, telemetry, and replay behavior

cases.prompt: Switch our NestJS service from Express to Fastify because a benchmark says it is twice as fast.
expectations: Rejects generic benchmark evidence as sufficient
Profiles HTTP adapter contribution and audits middleware compatibility
Benchmarks representative routes before and after

cases.prompt: Our @Cron cleanup job runs six times after scaling the NestJS deployment.
expectations: Explains that every replica runs the schedule
Chooses a platform scheduler, dedicated replica, distributed lease, or unique queued job
Makes cleanup idempotent and observable

cases.prompt: A NestJS payment use case is called by HTTP and a queue consumer. Add consistent error handling.
expectations: Keeps application failures transport-neutral
Maps failures at each HTTP or message boundary
Defines stable safe errors, logging ownership, and retry classification

cases.prompt: Secure a multi-tenant NestJS endpoint that uses JWT, accepts filters, and returns TypeORM entities.
expectations: Separates authentication from resource and tenant authorization
Validates and bounds filters while using injection-safe persistence APIs
Verifies JWT claims and returns an allow-listed response contract without entity leakage

cases.prompt: Write tests for a pure pricing policy, its Nest provider token, and the PostgreSQL adapter. Use TestingModule for all of them.
expectations: Directly constructs the pure policy instead of requiring TestingModule
Uses TestingModule for provider wiring
Uses a realistic PostgreSQL integration test for adapter semantics

cases.prompt: Prepare a NestJS queue worker for rolling Kubernetes deployment without losing or duplicating critical jobs.
expectations: Defines readiness, intake stop, drain deadline, and resource closure
Assumes duplicate delivery and requires idempotent processing
Includes compatible rollout, telemetry, retry/dead-letter behavior, and rollback checks
